newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK activists to unite in vigil to mourn leader.
newsitem.headline: HK activists to unite in vigil to mourn leader.

text.p: Hong Kong activists said on Friday they were organising a candlelight vigil to mourn a colleague who died while protesting Japan's claims to a group of disputed islands in the East China Sea.

"The vigil is to give our last respects to David Chan, and all Hong Kong organisations fighting to protect the Diaoyus will come together," said Ng Siu Wah of the Alliance of Worldwide Chinese For the Protection of the Diaoyu Islands.
The vigil this Sunday is expected to rally up to 20,000 Hong Kong people across three football fields at Victoria Park, organisers said.

Chan, leader of 18 activists who were aboard the protest ship Kien Hwa 2, drowned on Thursday after leaping into the stormy sea in defiance of a blockade of the disputed islands by Japanese coastguard patrol boats.
Chan's death was the first in almost two months of protests to sweep through Hong Kong, China, Taiwan and Macau since Japanese extremists built a lighthouse and raised Japanese flags on the islands.
Japan has claimed sovereign rights to the islands and refused to acknowledge that the dispute is still open for discussion with China.

Tokyo's claim to what it calls the Senkaku Islands dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries, referring to them as the Diaoyu Isles.
At least six organisations have sprouted in Hong Kong in recent weeks in a wave of nationalistic fervour to challenge Japan's claims, and organisers said the vigil would unite them.

"Whatever differences we might have, we are united in this one cause...his (Chan's) aim of protecting the Diaoyus is everyone's aim," said Tsang Yok-sing of the Hong Kong Universal Alliance for Protection of the Diaoyu Islands.
